content:
Facts: Daughter brought action to contest will and claim reserved share more than ten years after father’s death and designated heir’s acceptance, arguing she only recently learned of death.
Legal Framework: Art. 537 Civil Code (reserved portions); Art. 2934 Civil Code (imprescriptibility); Art. 2946 Civil Code (ten-year limitation period); prohibition of succession agreements.
Interpretative Issues: Whether reduction action is subject to limitation period; when limitation period begins to run; whether legitimate heir’s lack of knowledge about succession opening affects limitation period.
Legal Principles: Reduction action, being personal in nature, is subject to ordinary ten-year limitation period starting from succession opening. Right to reinstatement of reserved share is not imprescriptible under Art. 2934 Civil Code, as prohibition of succession agreements applies only to unopened successions; after opening, legitimate heir’s rights are freely available. Limitation period runs from succession opening (or heir’s acceptance) regardless of when legitimate heir discovered infringement of reserved share. Legitimate heir’s ignorance of decedent’s death does not suspend or extend limitation period; vigilantibus, non dormientibus, iura succurrunt. Action brought after ten-year period without prior interruptive acts is inadmissible.
